newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds reversed initial gains late in the session to end weaker after U.S. Treasuries slipped in early trade.

Volumes were again very low in a skittish and vulnerable market, dealers said, with investors fully withdrawn and even market professionals unwilling to trade until new direction became more apparent.

"There is noithing doing until we get some idea of where we are headed next," one broker said. U.S. non-farm payrolls figures due on Friday would be the main focus, he added, for all those looking for clues on the U.S. interest rate outlook.
If the payrolls report failed to give clear indications one way or another, the current lull could extend into the next week, another broker warned.
With the Dutch share market steadying on the day, expected demand for short paper had not materialised, he said.

Spreads to Bunds remained largely steady, though the long yield discount narrowed slightly toward the end of the session. Dealers saw little reason to switch between the two markets under current conditions.
The recent curve steepening trend continued, with the 2-10 year spread moving out to 230 basis points.
The spread has moved out 15 basis points in the last four sessions, but in the longer term is set to flatten again, traders said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
